intro: Every alignment source we can reach, set side by side. Where our system and other people's datasets disagree is where to look first. The sources differ in how they handle silent letters, so two answers count as the same structure when they group the sounding letters alike and differ only in where silent letters sit.

notations.label: ARPA
notations.tip: ARPAbet, as in the CMU dictionary

board.agreeTip: Share of words both this source and our system cover where the sounding letters are grouped the same way

matrixTitle: How often each pair groups the letters the same way
matrixTip: Share of shared words where the two sources group the sounding letters the same way, silent-letter placement aside. Darker is more agreement. The small number is the words both cover.
sharesTip: What this source has in common with our system. Agreement between sources that share inputs counts for less.

headline.agree: of the words compared agree with every other source
headline.outvoted: words where every other source agrees against us
headline.majority: words where most sources differ from us
headline.note: Showing the words with the most disagreement first, plus a sample of agreeing ones.

outvoted.label: Outvoted
outvoted.tip: Words where every other source differs from our answer

most.label: Most disagree
most.tip: Words where more than half the other sources differ

relation.structure: same units, silent letters placed differently

empty: Pick a word to see every source's answer.
silentTip: A letter that makes no sound here
structureOnly: This source only marks which letters carry a sound, so its sounds are not shown.
patternsTitle: Most common ways our answer differs from another source
patternsTip: Each chip is one repeated difference: our grouping on the left, theirs on the right, with how many words show it. Click one to see those words. Many are conventions (how a final al or ly is split), and the rest are places to look for mistakes.
title: Source comparison
